source.survey_title: Diving into Reliable Self-Evolving Agents: A Survey
source.principle: Classify each transition by the deepest evolution target whose active semantic change affects a decision-relevant output, update, or judgment, not by the algorithm name, training stage, or runtime components.

collections.label: Surveys and Positioning
collections.description: Surveys and adjacent literature used to position the field; these works are not assigned an L0-L4 self-evolution level.

collections.label: Cross-Level Reliability: Evidence, Acceptance, and Control
collections.description: Works supporting the survey's cross-level synthesis of shared failure modes, external audit signals, promotion reliability, and audit independence under compromise.

collections.label: Open Problems and Outlook
collections.description: Works cited in the research agenda on capability growth, longitudinal and adaptive evaluation, deployment, and scalable oversight.

levels.label: Output-Level Self-Evolution
levels.summary: changes the current output or trajectory while retained agent state remains unchanged across independent tasks.
levels.persistence: Task-local; retained agent state remains unchanged across independent tasks.

levels.label: Model-Level Self-Evolution
levels.summary: retains a change to trainable model or policy state that affects later task execution.
levels.persistence: The model or policy change affects later independent tasks.

levels.label: Scaffold-Level Self-Evolution
levels.summary: retains a change to prompts, tools, memory operations, workflows, topology, skills, or the runtime harness.
levels.persistence: The scaffold change affects later execution or retained evidence.

levels.label: Improver-Level Self-Evolution
levels.summary: retains a change to how later candidates are proposed, selected, committed, or rolled back.
levels.persistence: The changed improver governs future updates.

levels.label: Criterion-Level Self-Evolution
levels.summary: retains a change to judgment tasks, rewards, evaluator protocols, comparison rules, constraints, or values.
levels.persistence: The revised criterion governs later judgments.

classification_statuses.description: The system directly satisfies the retained rewrite semantics of its assigned level.
The core transition is shallower, but the work is discussed at a deeper frontier such as an adaptive curriculum or evaluator.
The system contains multiple active update paths; primary level records the deepest demonstrated rewrite.
The work is retained as an explicit classification boundary or ambiguous case.
The work supports positioning, reliability, evaluation, safety, or open problems rather than instantiating an L0-L4 system.
